Unfold EEMs into a matrix of samples and wavelength pairs

Source: R/data_functions.R
eem2mat.Rd

Each EEM in an eemlist is unfolded into a vector. The result is a matrix with one row per sample and one column per pair of excitation and emission wavelengths. This matrix is the input for the self-organising map in eemsom. The unfolding can be reversed by mat2eem.

Usage

eem2mat(eem_list, normalise = "sd", na = "remove")

Arguments

eem_list

object of class eemlist. All EEMs need to have the same excitation and emission wavelengths and unique sample names.

normalise

normalisation of each sample: "sd" (default) divides each EEM by its standard deviation like norm_array, "max" by its maximum (Ejarque-Gonzalez and Butturini 2014), "sum" by the sum of its fluorescence and "none" keeps the original values.

na

handling of missing values (e.g. removed scatter): "remove" (default) removes wavelength pairs that are missing in at least one sample, "keep" keeps wavelength pairs that are missing in some of the samples. Wavelength pairs that are missing in all samples are always removed, see details.

Value

A matrix with samples in rows and wavelength pairs in columns. Attributes: ex and em (wavelengths of the original EEMs), keep (logical vector stating which of the unfolded wavelength pairs are columns of the matrix), samples, normalise and norm_factors.

Details

Columns are named "ex|em", e.g. "250|450". The EEM matrix is unfolded column-wise, so emission wavelengths change faster than excitation wavelengths.

Normalisation removes differences in concentration and focuses on the shape of the EEMs. The normalisation factors are calculated from the remaining wavelength pairs (after removing missing values) and are saved as an attribute. They need to be positive, so EEMs with a maximum or a sum of zero or below cannot be normalised with "max" or "sum".

Wavelength pairs that are missing in all samples (e.g. scatter that was removed but not interpolated) carry no information and are removed even with na = "keep". Otherwise, the self-organising map would contain arbitrary values for them, because kohonen fills missing values in the initial codebook vectors with random values. With na = "keep", kohonen calculates the distances between samples and codebook vectors from the available wavelength pairs and scales them up to the number of all wavelength pairs.

References

Ejarque-Gonzalez, E., Butturini, A. (2014). Self-Organising Maps and Correlation Analysis as a Tool to Explore Patterns in Excitation-Emission Matrix Data Sets and to Discriminate Dissolved Organic Matter Fluorescence Components. PLoS ONE 9(6), e99618. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0099618

See also

mat2eem, eem2array

Other self-organising maps: eempf_som(), eemsom(), mat2eem()

Examples

data(eem_list)

m <- eem2mat(eem_list)
dim(m)
#> [1]   15 4554
attr(m, "norm_factors")
#>     d0680sfK      d1266sf     d1268sfK     d1543sfK     d1549sfK     d1550sfK 
#>   0.08683636   0.08967149   0.09703871   0.06498094   0.04673046   0.05382821 
#>     d1557sfK     d1559sfK     d1565sfK     d1567sfK     d1568sfK       d492sf 
#>   0.05307236   0.03873703   0.04166047   0.09772790   0.05926670   0.06871059 
#>       d661sf       d667sf dSFB445pwd1t 
#>   0.06043481   0.07290243   0.11637892
